system.name: CIAR
system.one_liner: Cloud-device collaborative decoding for autoregressive image generation: an on-device uncertainty quantifier over probability intervals and interval-enhanced decoding cut latency.

content.variant_note: a motivation panel of pie and bar charts, then three decoding frameworks drawn as identical layer stacks, each lane adding one component and topped by a clock badge
content.argues: Most tokens already match the device's top-probability choice, yet dropping verification hurts quality; CIAR's Inter-Head with cloud-device collaboration cuts generation time from 11.8 s to 4.67 s.
content.subject: Token acceptance statistics and three decoding frameworks (baseline, Lantern, CIAR) drawn as Transformer-layer stacks with latencies.

lessons.what_to_learn: Put a small measured motivation panel (pie and dual-axis bars) next to a row of identical layer-stack lanes that add one component each, and hang a clock badge with seconds and percentage saved above every lane so the efficiency claim is read first.
lessons.suits: Inference-acceleration or efficiency methods compared with a baseline and one prior method on latency and quality.

evidence: approximately 70% tokens approved by the cloud already match the device’s top-output
From left to right: baseline, Lantern, and our CIAR with Inter-Head and cloud-device collaboration

summary: CIAR is a cloud-device collaboration framework that speeds up autoregressive image generation with an on-device token uncertainty quantifier built on probability intervals. Figure 1 has two panels. Panel (a) motivates the design: a pie chart shows that about 70% of tokens already match the max-probability token, and a dual-axis bar chart gives CLIP and FID for Base, Lantern and Lantern without cloud verification, the last being clearly worse. Panel (b) draws three decoding frameworks (baseline, Lantern, CIAR, named only in the caption) as the same vertical stack of Transformer Layers x N under an LM Head, with a second small stack added in Lantern (verify arrow) and CIAR (Inter-Head Output). Clock badges give 11.8 s, 7.12 s (down 39%) and 4.67 s (down 60%).
summary_zh: CIAR 用端云协同加速自回归图像生成。图 1 左侧用饼图和柱状图说明约 70% 的词元可在端侧决定，右侧并排画出基线、Lantern 与 CIAR 三种解码结构，上方时钟标出 11.8、7.12、4.67 秒。
notes: The pre-screen listed side-by-side-contrast and model-anatomy; concept-schematic was added for panel (a), which is a motivation analysis. The lanes carry no names in the drawing and the role of the second stack (device or cloud side), the dark-grey squares and the dashed return line is not labelled, so those are described by appearance only (role null). The bar chart is a 103x76 pt bitmap per the digest; the pie is vector.
